title: Key squares

D0.outcome: Explains key squares: if the attacking king reaches one, the pawn queens whoever is to move.

D1.outcome: Given a pawn on a rank, marks its key squares.

D2.outcome: In unlabeled K+P positions, predicts the result with the key-square rule, including the rook-pawn exception and who is to move.

D3.outcome: Compares the key-square and opposition methods on the same position, and explains why the sixth-rank rule is a special case.

misconceptions: King directly in front of the pawn means it cannot be won (a rule of thumb).
sources: sources/sheets/capablanca_chess-fundamentals.md §7 row 6 (replace the rule of thumb with key squares)
conditions: Key squares as the primary rule; the sixth-rank threshold is a special case.
contrasts: The 'king directly in front means no win' rule of thumb treated as exact.
The sixth-rank opposition rule misses cases the key-square rule handles.
A position with additional pieces, where key squares alone do not decide.
